newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seventeen North Koreans seek asylum in South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Seventeen North Koreans seek asylum in South Korea.

text.p: A group of 17 North Koreans have fled the communist country to Hong Kong and are seeking asylum in South Korea, a Seoul foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
All but one of the 17, which include five children, are relatives. The other defector is a North Korean security official, the spokesman told reporters.
It would be the largest ever group defection to South Korea from the communist North.

The 17 sneaked into China on October 26 and crossed into Hong Kong on November 23. They were helped by ethnic Koreans in China, who were paid to act as guides by relatives of the North Koreans living in the United States, the spokesman said.
One of the defectors is the daughter of Choi Young-do, a defector now living in the United States, he said.
The previous largest defection was in 1987 when North Korean doctor Kim Man-chol, his wife and nine other relatives came to the South via a third country.
